Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

misc.tutorials (development version)

  • antigravity arrives from vscode.tutorials, shortened to a sign-in-and-try-it tutorial at ordering 1. Every other tutorial’s ordering moves up by one.

  • The R4DS family now has a deliberate pacing gradient. r4ds-1 and r4ds-2 open with four slow Introduction exercises, the lowercase-name warning and a spelled-out download.file(). r4ds-3 and r4ds-4 keep the standard three-exercise Introduction. From r4ds-5 on the Introduction is two exercises: one creates the repo, analysis.qmd, .gitignore and the libraries chunk, the other the data/ directory.

  • Three tutorials now teach the Codespace itself, a recorded departure from the base guide’s environment-neutral rule. In r4ds-5 the student downloads the data file to their own computer and drags or pastes it into the Codespace. In r4ds-6 three exercises tour /workspaces with pwd, ls .., ls -a and cd. In r4ds-7 the student runs connect-repo a second time to make r4ds-7-new, switches folders with File -> Open Folder..., and then deletes the extra repo both locally and on GitHub. In r4ds-8 two exercises review the picture with ls /workspaces and git remote -v.

  • census-1 is split in two. census-1 keeps the Texas income map and adds two exercises on the margin of error: a table of the counties where it is largest relative to the estimate, and a second map of that share. The new census-2 takes the state education chart and the California age scatterplot, with the scatterplot’s log scale now a step of its own. They run 17 and 18 exercises instead of 28.

  • The R4DS family is renumbered r4ds-1 through r4ds-10, each spin-out in the slot after its parent: music is now r4ds-2, the old r4ds-2 (births) is r4ds-3, nba-recruits is r4ds-4, the old r4ds-3 (school districts) is r4ds-5, time-use is r4ds-6, the old r4ds-4 (crypto) is r4ds-7, prediction-markets is r4ds-8, the old r4ds-5 (wildfires) is r4ds-9, and imdb-rankings is r4ds-10. Titles follow (“R4DS 2” and so on), as do the repo names and download URLs inside each tutorial. The introductory scaffolding moved with the slots: r4ds-2 now spells out the data/ commands and the download.file() call, and r4ds-3 (births) uses the goal-stated form like every later tutorial. Older entries below use the names current when they were written.

  • The census tutorials’ folders are census-1 and census-2 (formerly census and demographics), so their order is visible at a glance; their titles stay Mapping Census Data and Census Demographics. The list order is r4ds-1 to r4ds-10, then census-1 and census-2, then the topic tutorials.

  • Every Summary now ends the same way. Its first exercise is a final render, commit and push, answered with the URL of analysis.qmd (or index.qmd) on GitHub; that link is the record of the whole file. The whole-file show_file("analysis.qmd") paste is gone: with no chunk argument, show_file() prints only the last chunk, so the whole-file answer shown after Continue never matched what students saw. The separate repo-URL exercise is gone too, since the file URL contains it.

  • Every commit question asks for git log --oneline -3. The three census questions that accepted “a short note describing how you committed and pushed” now do too.

  • No tutorial explains how to take a screenshot any more. That sentence belongs to the first three vscode.tutorials; every screenshot question here just asks for the screenshot.

  • Editorial pass over every tutorial: prose has almost no semicolons and filler sentences are gone. No exercise asked for two pastes, so none were split. The repo line no longer says “You may need to restart this tutorial after you do so,” which was a learnr artifact.

  • Every code block now says what it is: commands carry their language (r, bash, yaml), text to type that is in no language (commit messages, .gitignore lines, download URLs) is default, and transcripts and the answers shown after Continue are {.output}, which renders lighter and without a copy button. The 376 bare fences are gone, so learnr2::check_tutorial() runs clean.

  • Every screenshot question is image-only (allow_text = FALSE), and the first one in each tutorial says how to take a screenshot and paste it. Needs the learnr2 that ships allow_text.

  • The R for Data Science material is now ten tutorials instead of five. Each two-topic tutorial was split in two, keeping its first topic and spinning the second out under a topic name: r4ds-1 (Billboard) and music, r4ds-2 (US births) and nba-recruits, r4ds-3 (school districts) and time-use, r4ds-5 (wildfires) and imdb-rankings. With prediction-markets (split from r4ds-4 in August) the family runs 18–25 exercises per tutorial, and the VS Code list shows each spin-out directly after its parent (ordering 1–10), followed by census-1, baseball, ducks, sharks, and movies.

  • spiderman is retired; its Spider-Man comparison is now the closing topic of movies.

  • ducks and sharks are rebuilt on the multi-page website form that baseball introduced, and every tutorial now follows the three-exercise caching arc exactly once. census-1 and baseball were shortened as well; every tutorial now runs 18–28 exercises.

  • Package-wide clean-up: every question carries a complete plain-text copy of its prompt; faked listings include the AGENTS.md that every fresh repo contains; faked git log and quarto publish transcripts match their real shape; knowledge drops are trimmed to two sentences about the data or the output; retired AI-tool recommendations are replaced by “Use AI however you like.”; stale quarto preview instructions and maintainer comments are gone.

  • r4ds-1 ships billboard.csv (a copy of tidyr::billboard) instead of loading the data from a package; r4ds-3 and time-use have students gitignore their .duckdb files; sharks no longer ships attacks.csv or attacks.rds.

  • Rebuilt every tutorial on learnr2, which renders each one to a static Quarto page whose code runs in the browser via WebR. learnr2 is the package’s only tutorial dependency (it also supplies show_file()), and the tests and CI render tutorials with learnr2::check_tutorial() and learnr2::render_tutorials(). Plot exercises now ask for a screenshot of the rendered plot instead of the code that drew it.

misc.tutorials 0.0.1

  • Initial release.

  • Contains the R for Data Science tutorials (r4ds-1 through r4ds-5) and the census tutorial, migrated from the vscode.tutorials package.
